area: settings (imaging / calibration / calibration-library / dark-library / captured-images / image-grading / adaptive-exposure / adaptive-conditions / preflight / autofocus / focus model)

units_unreached.why: Unreachable BY DESIGN FAULT, not by budget: no SettingsSectionDef with key 'focus-model' is built (settings_catalog.dart:591-678) and the alias kMergedSectionAliases['focus-model']='autofocus' (settings_catalog.dart:692) redirects to the Autofocus page, which mounts only AutofocusSettingsPage + PredictiveAfSettingsPage (merged_sections.dart:110-125). I drove the whole Autofocus page top-to-bottom (crop80/81/82/83/84) and there is no focus-model section. Reported as a defect below.

Reached and rendered, but only its gated empty state ('Connect to a remote appliance to browse its captured frames'). The grid, thumbnails and metadata rows are remote-only (backendProvider must be a NetworkBackend); no appliance was available on this sandbox, so the thumbnail/download paths were not exercised.

findings.title: Two settings pages disagree about whether a filter wheel exists; per-filter adaptive-exposure limits become unreachable
findings.what_happened: With the Simulated Filter Wheel connected (log: 'Simulator connected: id=sim_filterwheel_1 type=FilterWheel', 15:04:48), Settings > Equipment > Autofocus > 'Autofocus Filter Settings' lists 7 filters (L, R, G, B, Ha, OIII, SII), while Settings > Imaging > Adaptive Exposure > 'Per-filter overrides' shows a warning banner 'No filter wheel on active profile - adaptive applies to every capture (mono camera assumption).' The per-filter min/max/enable editor is replaced by that banner, so per-filter adaptive limits cannot be configured at all.
findings.expected: Both pages read the same source of truth. If a filter wheel is connected with named filters, Adaptive Exposure must offer the per-filter editor for those filters (or at minimum say 'no equipment profile saved' rather than asserting there is no filter wheel).
findings.repro: Fresh profile, Skip onboarding. Equipment > 'I'll do it manually' > Discovery Expand > Filter Wheels > Connect (Simulated Filter Wheel). Settings > Imaging > Adaptive Exposure > enable 'Enable global default' -> banner says no filter wheel. Settings > Equipment > Autofocus, scroll to 'Autofocus Filter Settings' -> 7 filters listed.
findings.proposed_fix: Make the adaptive-exposure per-filter editor fall back to filterWheelStateProvider.filterNames when the active profile has none (same precedence the Autofocus page uses), and reword the banner to name the real cause ('No filter wheel connected and no filters on the active profile').
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live on display :82, profile settings-imaging-verify, fresh. Connected Simulated Filter Wheel (app.log 15:14:27 'Simulator connected: id=sim_filterwheel_1 type=FilterWheel'). Settings > Equipment > Autofocus > Autofocus Filter Settings lists 7 rows L/R/G/B/Ha/OIII/SII (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/siv-16-af-scroll.png) while Settings > Imaging > Adaptive Exposure shows the banner 'No filter wheel on active profile - adaptive applies to every capture (mono camera assumption).' (siv-13-ae-on.png). Code claim is exact: adaptive_exposure_settings.dart:315-316 reads activeEquipmentProfileProvider?.filterNames; autofocus_settings.dart:128,756-760 reads filterWheelStateProvider.filterNames. I went further than the reporter: after using discovery 'Assign' to attach the wheel to the active profile (profile card then reads '1 devices', status '1 connected', sqlite equipment_profiles.filter_names still empty), the banner PERSISTS (siv-22-ae3.png) - at that point the banner's literal statement is false, because the profile does have a filter wheel. HOWEVER the strongest claim ('per-filter adaptive limits cannot be configured at all') is overstated: Equipment > Edit Profile > Filters (0 slots) > 'Auto-detect from wheel' > Save Changes writes filter_names=["L","R","G","B","Ha","OIII","SII"] and the per-filter min/max/enable editor then renders all 7 rows (siv-27-ae4.png). So this is a source-of-truth/discoverability defect with a false banner, not an unreachable feature. Severity corrected P1 -> P2.

findings.title: 'Auto dark subtraction' in Dark Library is the same switch as 'Auto-calibrate light frames' - turning it off silently kills flat and bias correction too
findings.what_happened: Settings > Equipment > Dark Library > 'Auto dark subtraction' ('Automatically subtract matching darks from light frames') and Settings > Equipment > Calibration > 'Auto-calibrate light frames' ('Apply dark, flat, and bias correction to captured images automatically') are one and the same setting (calibration.auto_calibrate). I switched OFF 'Auto dark subtraction' on the Dark Library page; the DB key calibration.auto_calibrate flipped true->false and the Calibration page's 'Auto-calibrate light frames' was then also OFF.
findings.expected: A control labelled 'Auto dark subtraction' must control dark subtraction only, or be labelled to say it is the master calibration switch. As shipped, a user who wants darks off but flats on has no way to express that and is not told what they just switched off.
findings.repro: Settings > Equipment > Calibration: turn 'Auto-calibrate light frames' ON (DB calibration.auto_calibrate=true). Settings > Equipment > Dark Library: turn 'Auto dark subtraction' OFF. sqlite3 .../skotiq.db "select value from app_settings where key='calibration.auto_calibrate'" -> false. Return to Calibration: 'Auto-calibrate light frames' is OFF.
findings.proposed_fix: Either rename the Dark Library row to 'Auto-calibrate light frames (dark, flat, bias)' and mirror the Calibration subtitle verbatim, or split it into a real per-frame-type gate. Do not keep one boolean behind two contradictory labels.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Settings > Equipment > Calibration: turned 'Auto-calibrate light frames' ON -> sqlite app_settings calibration.auto_calibrate=true. Settings > Equipment > Dark Library then showed 'Auto dark subtraction' already ON (siv-30-darklib.png), i.e. one boolean behind two labels. Turned it OFF there -> calibration.auto_calibrate=false and the Calibration page's 'Auto-calibrate light frames' is OFF (siv-31-cal-after.png). Code path confirmed: dark_library_settings.dart:81-91 -> DarkLibrarySettingsActions.setAutoCalibrate (dark_library_provider.dart:357-364) -> CalibrationSettingsNotifier.setAutoCalibrate; the read at dark_library_provider.dart:322 is stored['calibration.auto_calibrate']. The consequence also holds: imaging_service.dart:582 gates the ENTIRE calibrateFile() call (which returns darkApplied/flatApplied/biasApplied) on calSettings.autoCalibrate, so switching off 'Auto dark subtraction' does disable flat and bias correction. Severity corrected P1 -> P2: nothing is lost (the uncalibrated FITS is still written and the raw frames survive); the defect is a mislabeled control that silently widens its scope.

findings.title: File naming pattern accepts unknown variables and path-traversal segments with no validation; the failure only surfaces at capture time
findings.what_happened: Settings > Imaging > 'File naming pattern' accepted and persisted '../../../pwned/$NOPE' and later '$TARGET_$BANANA' with no error, no warning and no preview. DB app_settings.file_naming_pattern held the literal strings. The capture pipeline rejects both: expandNamingPattern throws ValidationException for unknown tokens and buildImageFilePath throws for '..' segments - i.e. every frame of the night fails to be written, and the user is only told when the first exposure completes.
findings.expected: Validate on commit: reject unknown $TOKENs and unsafe path segments in the settings field (the pipeline already has the token set and the segment rules), and show the resolved example filename live like NINA does.
findings.repro: Settings > Imaging > click the 'File naming pattern' field, Ctrl+A, type '$TARGET_$BANANA', Enter. Field shows '$TARGET_$BANANA' in normal (non-error) styling. sqlite3 .../skotiq.db "select value from app_settings where key='file_naming_pattern'" -> $TARGET_$BANANA.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-imaging-12-pattern.png (../../../pwned/$NOPE accepted) and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-imaging-115-pattern-banana.png (crop115.png); DB output 'file_naming_pattern|$TARGET_$BANANA'. NOTE: the capture-time throw was NOT observed live - desktop 'Snapshot' is preview-only (badge 'Preview only' in /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-imaging-123-snap2.png, Session 'Captured 0 frames', empty /tmp/ns-audit/settings-imaging/captures/), so triggering it needs a full sequence run which was outside this area. The throw is read at the named lines.
findings.proposed_fix: Reuse ImagingService._patternVariables and the segment rules in a SettingsTextInput validator so the field refuses to commit an invalid pattern, and render a live 'M31/Light/M31_L_120s_0001.fits' preview under the row.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced: Settings > Imaging > File naming pattern, Ctrl+A, typed '../../../pwned/$NOPE', Enter. Field renders the value in normal (non-error) styling with no warning and no preview (siv-35-pattern-bad.png); sqlite app_settings.file_naming_pattern = '../../../pwned/$NOPE'. Code claims verified: imaging_settings.dart:63-83 wires SettingsTextInput straight to setFileNamingPattern with no validator, and settings_sections/imaging.dart:36-39 persists whatever it is given. The consequence chain is real: namingPatternProvider (imaging_provider.dart:288-294) reads settings.fileNamingPattern -> _generateImageFilePath (imaging_service/file_paths.dart:50) -> buildImageFilePath, which throws ValidationException for unknown $TOKENs (imaging_service.dart ~1057-1067) and for '..'/empty/unsafe segments (~1131-1143); the comment at imaging_service.dart:400-403 states file-path failure 'fails the capture and stops loop callers'. Existing tests (imaging_service_test.dart:2479, 2500) already assert both throws. CORRECTION to the framing: there is no path traversal - the pipeline rejects '..' segments and additionally enforces path.isWithin(basePath, candidate), so 'path-traversal' overstates it. This is a deferred-error validation gap, not a security hole. Severity corrected P1 -> P2.

findings.title: 'Focus Model' settings page is fully built but is not mounted anywhere - the temp-compensation model viewer is unreachable, and the settings index is out of lock-step
findings.what_happened: focus_model_settings.dart (310 lines: pulls the appliance's temperature-compensation model - slope, R2, reliability - over REST and offers a Clear action) has no SettingsSectionDef. buildSettingsGroups' Advanced group builds logs/backup/updates/rig-catalogs/captured-images/replay-debug only. The alias map sends 'focus-model' deep links to 'autofocus', whose page (driven end-to-end) contains only AUTOFOCUS + PREDICTIVE AUTOFOCUS. Separately, _structuralGroups still lists 'focus-model' as an Advanced section key, so the derived kSettingsSectionIndex assigns 'replay-debug' an index one higher than its real catalog position.
findings.expected: Either surface the page (Advanced > Focus Model, gated on a remote backend the way Captured Images is) or delete it and drop the alias and the phantom _structuralGroups entry. Also: searching 'focus model' in Settings matches the Autofocus section (its keywords include 'focus model' and 'temperature compensation'), landing the user on a page that has neither - and app_settings still stores temp_compensation and temp_coefficient (-12.0) with no UI anywhere in the Autofocus page to edit them.
findings.repro: Settings > Equipment > Autofocus; scroll the entire page (two sections: AUTOFOCUS, PREDICTIVE AUTOFOCUS, ending at 'Learned models'). No focus-model / temperature-compensation controls. Settings search 'gain' likewise returns Imaging, which has no gain control.
findings.evidence: source-only for the catalog wiring; live evidence that the Autofocus page has no focus-model section: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-imaging-80-autofocus.png, -81-af2.png, -82-af3.png, -83-af4.png, -84-af5.png. Live evidence of the misleading search: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-imaging-11-search-gain.png
findings.proposed_fix: Add the section to the Advanced group next to captured-images, remove 'focus-model' from kMergedSectionAliases, and delete the phantom key from _structuralGroups so kSettingsSectionIndex matches the built catalog.

findings.title: Adaptive Conditions accepts all-zero score weights and calls it a readability preference; it actually switches the feature off
findings.what_happened: I set transparency/seeing/cloud/wind weights all to 0 (each field's min is 0, and there is no floor on the total). The page persisted {"transparency":0.0,"seeing":0.0,"cloud":0.0,"wind":0.0} and displayed: 'Weights sum to 0.00. The composer renormalizes available axes at runtime, but keeping the total near 1.00 makes the score easier to reason about.' That message is untrue for a zero total: AdaptiveSwapService.compose returns null when weightTotal <= 0, so no conditions score is ever produced and adaptive target swapping silently degrades to 'ConditionsUnknown' forever.
findings.expected: Either refuse to commit a configuration whose total is 0, or say what actually happens: 'All weights are zero - no conditions score can be computed and adaptive swapping will not run.'
findings.repro: Settings > Automation & Safety > Adaptive Conditions > Score weights: set each of the four fields to 0 (click, Ctrl+A, type 0, Enter).
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/adaptive_conditions_settings.dart:65-68 and :271-273 (min:0, no total floor); packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/adaptive_swap_service.dart:174 ('if (weightTotal <= 0) return null;')
findings.proposed_fix: Clamp the commit so at least one weight is > 0, and change the warning copy for the zero case to state that the score cannot be computed.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim. Settings > Automation & Safety > Adaptive Conditions, set all four weights to 0 -> sqlite adaptive_swap.score_weights = {"transparency":0.0,"seeing":0.0,"cloud":0.0,"wind":0.0} and the callout reads exactly 'Weights sum to 0.00. The composer renormalizes available axes at runtime, but keeping the total near 1.00 makes the score easier to reason about.' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/siv-39-callout.png). Code confirmed: adaptive_conditions_settings.dart _ScoreWeightRow uses min:0 with no total floor, and _WeightTotalCallout branches only on nearOne (|total-1|<0.001) so the zero case falls into the generic 'renormalizes' copy. adaptive_swap_service.dart:174 is 'if (weightTotal <= 0) return null;' and AdaptiveSwapDriver.tick (line ~272) pushes that null straight to sequencerUpdateConditionsScore, so no conditions score ever reaches the Rust decision path (AdaptiveSwapDecision::ConditionsUnknown, adaptive_swap.rs:306/318). The copy is therefore untrue for a zero total. P2 stands - this is the 'app states something untrue' class, though it requires a deliberate all-zero config on a feature whose 'Enabled for new schedulers' toggle is off by default.

findings.title: Pre-flight preview card contradicts itself when the polar-alignment check is disabled
findings.what_happened: With strictness = Strict and 'Polar alignment max age' = 0, the 'What this will do at sequence start' card prints both 'Sequence start is blocked on: missing darks for the planned exposures, time drift > 30s, stale polar alignment, focuser at travel limit.' and 'Polar alignment age check is disabled (set max age above 0 to enable).' The card exists specifically to tell the user what will happen, and it names a check that is switched off.
findings.expected: The strictness bullet should be composed from the live configuration - drop 'stale polar alignment' from the blocking list when polarAgeDays == 0.
findings.repro: Settings > Automation & Safety > Pre-flight Checks: set 'Polar alignment max age' to 0, then select Strict.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/preflight_settings.dart:226-254 (static per-strictness bullets, then an independent polarAgeDays bullet)
findings.proposed_fix: Build the bullet list conditionally on polarAgeDays > 0 instead of emitting both.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim. Settings > Automation & Safety > Pre-flight Checks, set 'Polar alignment max age' to 0, selected Strict. The single 'What this will do at sequence start' card prints both 'Sequence start is blocked on: missing darks for the planned exposures, time drift > 30s, stale polar alignment, focuser at travel limit.' AND 'Polar alignment age check is disabled (set max age above 0 to enable).' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/siv-41-preflight-strict.png). Code matches: preflight_settings.dart _LivePreviewCard emits static per-strictness bullets in the switch, then an independent polarAgeDays bullet. The 'disabled' half is the accurate one - preflight_rules.dart:550 is 'if (settings.polarAlignmentMaxAgeDays <= 0) return const [];' - so the strictness bullet is the false statement. Severity P3 as called.

findings.title: Image Grading: eccentricity max can be set to 1.00, which is a threshold the pipeline can never exceed - the check becomes inert with no warning
findings.what_happened: I typed 5 into 'Eccentricity max'; it clamped to 1.00 and persisted image_grading_eccentricity_threshold=1.0. Frame eccentricity is computed as sqrt(1 - lambda2/lambda1), which is strictly < 1.0 for any star with a finite minor axis, and the rule is 'reject if eccentricity exceeds this value' - so 1.00 can never fire. The UI gives no indication that the check is now dead. The same shape applies at the other end of several ranges: HFR absolute min 0.1 px (below any achievable HFR -> rejects every frame), HFR absolute max 50 px (never fires), star-count min max 100000 (rejects every frame on any realistic sensor).
findings.expected: Clamp eccentricity to something the detector can actually exceed (e.g. 0.99), or annotate the field when the value makes the check inert ('at 1.00 this check never fires'). Same for the HFR/star-count extremes.
findings.repro: Settings > Imaging > Image Grading: enable the master toggle, click 'Eccentricity max', Ctrl+A, type 5, Enter -> field shows 1.00, DB shows 1.0.
findings.proposed_fix: Cap at 0.99 and surface an inline note when a threshold is outside the range the pipeline can produce.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Mechanically reproduced: enabled the master toggle, typed 5 into 'Eccentricity max' -> field clamps to 1.00 and sqlite image_grading_eccentricity_threshold=1.0 (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/siv-43-ecc.png). UI range confirmed at image_grading_settings.dart:196-197 (min 0.0 / max 1.0); the other cited ranges are also as claimed (HFR absolute min 0.1 / max 50 at :150-151, star count min 1 / max 100000 at :217-218). The inertness holds, but NOT via the file the finding cites: difference_image.rs:865-876 moment_eccentricity is the transient-detection measure, not the grading path. The grading value is stats.rs:526 (sqrt(1 - lambda2/lambda1)) aggregated by frame_eccentricity (stats.rs:957-963), which explicitly filters to (0.0..=1.0), and image_grading.rs:200-201 compares 'ecc > threshold' - so at 1.00 the gate can never fire. Severity corrected P3 -> P4: 1.00 is the mathematical maximum of the metric, the field already documents 'Leave blank to disable', and clamping out-of-range input to the legal maximum is standard behaviour. This is a copy/annotation nit, not a defect that can cost data.

findings.title: Required-field error text is truncated to an unreadable stub
findings.what_happened: Clearing 'Max consecutive rejects' (allowClear:false) restores 3 and renders errorText 'A value is required.' inside a 140 px-wide field, where it clips to 'A value is requir...'. The user is told there is an error but not what it is.
findings.expected: Error text should render below the row at full width, not inside the fixed-width input.
findings.repro: Settings > Imaging > Image Grading (master toggle ON) > 'Max consecutive rejects': click, Ctrl+A, Delete, Enter.
findings.proposed_fix: Move the error string out of InputDecoration.errorText into a full-width Text under the SettingRow, as the adaptive-exposure page already does.

findings.title: 'Sensor W' field label is ellipsized to 'Sensor...' in Calibration Library's matching preview
findings.what_happened: In Settings > Imaging > Calibration Library > Matching Preview, the empty 'Sensor W' input renders its resting label as 'Sensor...' at width 90. The neighbouring 'Sensor H' fits, so the two fields cannot be told apart until one is filled (the floating label then shows in full).
findings.expected: Either widen the field or shorten the label to 'Sensor W (px)'/'W px' so it is legible when empty.
findings.repro: Settings > Imaging > Calibration Library, look at the Matching Preview field row.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-imaging-40-callib.png and crop41.png ('Sensor...'); crop43.png shows the full 'Sensor W' label only once a value is typed
findings.proposed_fix: Bump the width to 110 (as used for Exposure/Filter) or relabel.

findings.title: Settings > Imaging is called 'Default capture settings' and is indexed for gain/offset/binning/exposure, but contains none of them
findings.what_happened: The Imaging section renders exactly two rows: a read-only 'Archive format: FITS - 16-bit' and 'File naming pattern'. Its catalog keywords are ['exposure','gain','offset','binning','file format','fits','frame naming'], so searching 'gain' in Settings returns Imaging (plus Help & Tutorials, Image Grading, Science) - and none of those pages has a gain control. Default gain/offset/binning/cooling actually live in the onboarding 'Camera defaults' step / equipment profile, which the search never points at.
findings.expected: Either surface the profile's camera defaults on this page (or a deep link to Equipment Profiles), or strip the false keywords so search does not promise a control that isn't there.
findings.repro: Settings > search 'gain' -> Imaging is offered; open Imaging -> two rows, no gain.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a 'Capture defaults' section that surfaces the active profile's gain/offset/binning/cooling read-only with an 'Edit in Equipment Profiles' action, and keep the keywords.

findings.title: Backlash IN ships at 350 steps with method 'Overshoot' - an unmeasured, asymmetric mechanical default applied to every focuser
findings.what_happened: A freshly seeded profile has af_backlash_comp_method='Overshoot', af_backlash_in='350', af_backlash_out='0'. Backlash is a per-focuser mechanical property the app cannot know; 350 steps is comparable to the entire default AF sweep (step size 50 x 2 x initial offset 4 = 400 steps) and can exceed the usable travel of small stepper/Crayford focusers, so every AF move is perturbed - or clamped/errored - out of the box. The asymmetry (IN 350, OUT 0) has no physical justification either.
findings.expected: Ship 0/0 (no compensation) and provide a backlash-measurement helper, the way NINA does. A non-zero default silently changes where the focuser lands on the first night on unknown hardware.
findings.repro: Fresh profile (drive_linux.py start --fresh), Skip onboarding, Settings > Equipment > Autofocus. Also sqlite3 .../skotiq.db "select key,value from app_settings where key like 'af_backlash%'".
findings.proposed_fix: Default af_backlash_in and af_backlash_out to 0, and add a 'Measure backlash' action next to the Backlash compensation dropdown.

findings.title: Autofocus and Predictive AF express three key thresholds in raw focuser steps the app cannot interpret
findings.what_happened: Step size (50), Backlash IN (350) and Predictive AF 'Drift threshold (steps)' (200) are all raw focuser-step counts with no relation to the critical focus zone, steps-per-micron, or the focuser's travel range - none of which the page shows. On a focuser whose CFZ is ~30 steps the 200-step drift gate never warns; on one with 500 steps of total travel it always warns. Range maxima are equally uninformed (step size up to 10000, backlash up to 10000).
findings.expected: Show the connected focuser's max position/step size next to these fields and express drift as a fraction of the measured V-curve half-width (or in microns via a steps-per-micron input), so the numbers mean something. NINA and SGP both derive step size from a measured curve rather than a blind default.
findings.repro: Settings > Equipment > Autofocus (right column) and scroll to PREDICTIVE AUTOFOCUS > 'Drift threshold (steps)'.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the connected focuser's position range and a steps-per-micron field to the page, and label the drift threshold in both steps and the equivalent fraction of the fitted curve.

findings.title: Adaptive Exposure lengthens subs when the sky gets brighter - the opposite of the sub-exposure rule every other tool applies
findings.what_happened: The page states 'Lengthens or shortens each frame automatically when the sky is brighter or darker than your reference, so signal-to-noise stays roughly constant'. The implementation is ratio = 10^((mag_ref - mag_live)/2.5), so a brighter sky (lower mag) multiplies the exposure up. The module's own worked example admits the outcome: 60 s nominal at ref 21.5 becomes 499 s under a Bortle-6 19.2 sky, 'far too long for backyard tracking', and is then clamped. With shipped defaults (ref 21.5, max 600 s) any sky more than ~1 mag brighter than reference pins every sub at the 600 s ceiling all night. SharpCap/NINA/Dr. Glover's rule is the inverse: t proportional to 1/sky-rate, i.e. shorter subs under a brighter sky, to keep the sky from filling the well.
findings.expected: Either invert the scaling to the standard 'swamp read noise / fixed sky ADU' rule, or rename the feature and say plainly that it maximises per-frame SNR at the cost of longer, more loss-prone subs, and default it to a target sky-ADU rather than a magnitude reference.
findings.repro: Settings > Imaging > Adaptive Exposure, read the description and 'How it works' card; compare with the formula at the named line.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a 'target sky background (ADU or e-)' mode that scales t inversely with sky rate, make it the default, and keep the constant-SNR mode as an explicit opt-in.

findings.title: Reference sky brightness range 14-24 mag/arcsec2 admits values no real sky can reach, which pin the feature at its clamp forever
findings.what_happened: The 'Reference sky brightness' input clamps to [14, 24]. The darkest natural sky is ~22.0 mag/arcsec2. I typed 99 and it silently became 24.00 with no message. At ref = 24 against a typical 21.5 sky the ratio is 10^(2.5/2.5) = 10x, so every exposure is driven to the 'Longest exposure' clamp for the whole session; at ref = 14 every exposure sits on the 'Shortest exposure' clamp.
findings.expected: Restrict to a physically meaningful band (roughly 16-22.2) and tell the user when a typed value was clamped instead of silently rewriting it.
findings.repro: Settings > Imaging > Adaptive Exposure (enabled) > 'Reference sky brightness': click, Ctrl+A, type 99, Enter -> shows 24, no message.
findings.proposed_fix: Narrow the range and surface a 'clamped to N' hint on commit.

findings.title: Image Grading thresholds cannot be edited until the master toggle is armed, so enabling it arms scale-blind defaults immediately
findings.what_happened: With the shipped default (grading OFF) all five threshold fields render at 0.5 opacity inside an IgnorePointer, so they cannot be edited. The only way to tune them is to switch grading ON first - which immediately arms HFR absolute 3.50 px, eccentricity 0.70, star-count min 10 and 'pause after 3 consecutive rejects'. HFR in pixels is pixel-scale dependent: at ~0.4"/px (2000 mm, 3.76 um) 2.5" seeing gives HFR ~6 px, so every frame is rejected and the sequence pauses after three - a lost night from one switch flip.
findings.expected: Allow the thresholds to be edited while the master toggle is off (grey the section header, not the inputs), and express the HFR gate in arcseconds (or as a multiple of the measured baseline) so it is scale-independent. Keeping only the relative 'HFR baseline percent' check armed by default would be safer.
findings.repro: Fresh profile, Settings > Imaging > Image Grading: try to click 'HFR absolute (pixels)' with the master toggle off - the field does not take focus.
findings.proposed_fix: Drop the IgnorePointer, keep only the visual dimming, and switch the absolute HFR gate to arcseconds computed from the optical train.

findings.title: Default file naming pattern puts every frame of every target and every night in one flat directory, and the field documents 5 of 18 variables
findings.what_happened: The shipped default is '$TARGET_$FILTER_$DATE_$SEQ' with no '/' - so lights, and every target and every session, land side by side in the capture root. The row's subtitle advertises only '$TARGET, $FILTER, $DATE, $SEQ, $EXPOSURE'; the pipeline supports 18 tokens including $FRAMETYPE, $FRAMENUM, $EXPTIME, $TIME, $DATETIME, $GAIN, $OFFSET, $TEMP, $BINNING, $CAMERA, $TELESCOPE, $SEQUENCE, $SESSION. Nothing tells the user that '/' creates subdirectories - the single most-used feature of a naming pattern - even though the code's own default constant is '$TARGET/$FRAMETYPE/$TARGET_$FILTER_$EXPTIME_$FRAMENUM'.
findings.expected: Ship '$TARGET/$FRAMETYPE/$TARGET_$FILTER_$EXPTIME_$FRAMENUM' (the constant already in NamingPattern), list all supported variables in a popover, and state that '/' creates folders. NINA and SGP both default to target/date/filter folders.
findings.repro: Fresh profile, Settings > Imaging: pattern reads '$TARGET_$FILTER_$DATE_$SEQ', subtitle lists 5 variables.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/database/database/default_settings.dart:21 and packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/settings_sections/app_settings_state.dart:485 (default); packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/imaging_settings.dart:66-67 (subtitle); packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/imaging/imaging_models/naming_and_autofocus.dart:10,34-51 (the richer default and full variable list)
findings.proposed_fix: Change the seeded default to the subdirectory pattern and replace the 5-variable subtitle with a full variable reference plus a live filename preview.

findings.title: Dark Library has no way to add or import dark frames
findings.what_happened: The page offers Auto dark subtraction, temperature tolerance, statistics, Clean Orphans, Clear Library, Frame Groups and All Entries. The empty state says 'Capture dark or bias frames to populate the library' but there is no button anywhere on the page to start a dark-capture run, and no way to import an existing library of masters from disk. Everything on the page is destructive or read-only.
findings.expected: An 'Import darks...' file/folder picker and a 'Build dark library' action that seeds a dark-capture sequence, next to Clean Orphans / Clear Library. Every imager arriving from NINA/SGP already has a dark library on disk.
findings.repro: Settings > Equipment > Dark Library, scroll the whole page.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/dark_library_settings.dart (Library Management section: only Clean Orphans + Clear Library)
findings.proposed_fix: Add Import and Build actions to the Library Management row.

findings.title: 'Clear Library' is enabled and destructive when the library is empty, and its confirm dialog names no count and no path
findings.what_happened: With 0 dark frames, 0 bias frames and 0 masters, the red 'Clear Library' button is still enabled. Its dialog reads 'Remove all entries from the dark library?' with an 'Also delete files from disk' checkbox - it does not say how many entries, or which directory would be deleted from. Confirming produced the (correct and honest) result banner 'Library cleared (0 entries removed).'
findings.expected: Disable the button at 0 entries, and put the count and the on-disk root in the dialog ('Remove 47 entries? 47 files under /path will also be deleted').
findings.repro: Settings > Equipment > Dark Library (empty) > Clear Library.
findings.proposed_fix: Gate the button on _stats.total > 0 and interpolate the count + resolved path into the dialog body.

findings.title: 'Captured Images' is a remote-only image browser filed under Settings > Advanced, where it is permanently dead on desktop
findings.what_happened: On a local desktop backend the section renders one line: 'Connect to a remote appliance to browse its captured frames.' It is honest, but a thumbnail gallery is not a setting, and the row occupies a permanent slot in the Advanced nav for every desktop user who will never see content in it.
findings.expected: Hide the section when the backend is not a NetworkBackend (the app already knows), or move the browser into the Imaging/Session Review surface where a gallery belongs and leave a deep link in Settings.
findings.repro: Settings > Advanced > Captured Images on a local desktop instance.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/settings_catalog.dart:650-664; packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/captured_images_settings.dart:15-21 (doc comment already says 'Remote-only; the local desktop has its own image browser')
findings.proposed_fix: Filter the section out of the catalog when backendProvider is not a NetworkBackend, the same way the page already gates its body.

findings.title: Sequence checkpoints and logs are written to the platform app-support directory, ignoring the configured data directory
findings.unit: settings:captured-images (observed while auditing; owner is the sequencer/storage layer)
findings.what_happened: With SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR and SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR both pointed at /tmp/ns-audit/settings-imaging/data, the app logged 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop' and 'Log directory: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/logs'. skotiq_session.checkpoint in that shared directory was being rewritten by my sandboxed instance. The visible consequence: on entering the app I was offered 'Recover Sequence? ... New Sequence, Saved 0m ago, Completed 6 frames (0m integration)' for a sequence that does not exist in this profile's database (select * from sequence_checkpoints returned zero rows).
findings.expected: Checkpoint and log paths must follow the same data-directory resolution as the database, so a second profile/data-dir never reads or overwrites another instance's run state.
findings.repro: Start the app with SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR set to a scratch path; read /tmp/ns-audit/<profile>/app.log for the two 'directory' lines; ls -la ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/ shows skotiq_session.checkpoint mtime tracking the sandboxed run.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/settings-imaging/app.log lines at 13:54:14 ('Log directory: ...') and 13:54:15 ('Setting checkpoint directory to: ...'); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-imaging-04-skip.png (the phantom Recover dialog); sqlite3 output 'select * from sequence_checkpoints' -> empty
findings.where: source-only beyond the log lines - the checkpoint-directory call site is in the native bridge startup path, not in my area's Dart files
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the checkpoint and log roots from the same SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR-aware helper the database uses.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced independently in my own fresh instance. /proc/1436364/environ confirms SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/settings-imaging-verify/data, yet that instance's own log says 'Log directory: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/logs' (15:10:40) and 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop' (15:10:41). The visible consequence reproduced too: immediately after 'Skip onboarding' the app offered 'Recover Sequence? ... AUDIT SEQ, Saved 0m ago, Completed 2 frames' (siv-02-skip.png) for a sequence that does not exist in this profile - sqlite 'select count(*) from sequence_checkpoints' returns 0. The dialog is modal and Escape does not dismiss it, so the only exits are Resume (would run another instance's sequence) or Discard (I backed the shared file up first, clicked Discard, and restored it - which also proves the write side of the hazard). CORRECTION to the finding's 'where': the call site is NOT in the native bridge startup path, it is Dart - packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:346 calls backend.sequencerSetCheckpointDir(supportDir.path) with getApplicationSupportDirectory(), and apps/desktop/lib/desktop_logging_init.dart:60-68 pins the log dir the same way (configureSkotiqDataDirectory only fills SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR when it is unset, and the logDir/checkpoint paths never consult it at all). Severity P2 stands: for a single desktop instance the practical impact is only that a relocated data directory is not honoured, but the project documents running a headless daemon alongside a GUI on one host (main_headless with SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR), and in that supported configuration the two processes share one checkpoint file.

verified_correct: Adaptive Exposure min/max validation: setting Shortest exposure = 700 with Longest = 600 was rejected with 'Minimum exposure cannot exceed maximum exposure.', the field reverted to 5, and nothing was written to the DB. Changing Longest to 500 persisted correctly as adaptive_exposure_max_secs|500.0 (evidence: settings-imaging-21-ae-minmax.png). I attacked it with an inverted pair, an out-of-range magnitude (99 -> clamped to 24) and a re-edit after the error; the only complaint is that the stale error string lingers after you move to another field.

Calibration Library 'Preview auto-selection' is honest with an empty library: it reported 'Dark/Bias/Flat/Defect map: no match' plus 'Not signed in to a shared calibration hub - shared masters were not consulted; showing local masters only.' and named the exact query ('No matching master dark (gain 100, offset 50, bin 1x1, 300s) - dark subtraction will be skipped'). I tried to break its validation by filling Sensor W and leaving Sensor H blank and got 'Preview failed: Enter both sensor width and sensor height, or leave both blank.' (evidence: crop41.png, crop42.png, crop43.png).

Calibration page conditional UI: turning off 'Auto-match from dark library' correctly revealed a 'Manual dark frame' row AND updated the Dark status card from 'Library empty' to 'Manual - not set'; the toggle persisted as calibration.auto_dark_from_library|false (evidence: crop54.png).

Dark Library destructive actions report truthfully: 'Clear Library' on an empty library returned 'Library cleared (0 entries removed).' - a count, not a vague 'Done'. Temperature tolerance dropdown (0.5/1.0/1.5/2.0/3.0/5.0) persisted the selected 5.0 to dark_library.temp_tolerance (evidence: crop70.png, crop66.png, crop67.png).

Pre-flight Checks is the best-designed page in my scope: three strictness options with concrete consequences, and a live 'What this will do at sequence start' card that re-composes when you change strictness or the polar-alignment age. Strict and polar age 0 both persisted (preflight_strictness|strict, polar_alignment_max_age_days|0). I attacked it by setting the age to 0 while Strict - the only flaw found is the self-contradicting bullet reported above (evidence: crop95.png, crop96.png).

Adaptive Conditions weight feedback is live and specific: with the shipped 0.4/0.25/0.25/0.1 it says 'Weights sum to 1.00. The composer will preserve the configured balance.' and flips to an amber warning the moment the total moves. Score floor 50 and hysteresis 180 s persisted correctly (evidence: crop99.png, crop100.png).

Image Grading numeric commit semantics are correct: out-of-range input is clamped and canonicalised (5 -> 1.00), blank commits null on the optional thresholds, and a required field that is cleared restores its previous value rather than writing garbage (evidence: crop31.png).

Settings persistence generally: every control I changed in my sections was verified against sqlite3 app_settings rather than trusted from the UI - file_naming_pattern, image_output_path, adaptive_exposure_{enabled,reference_mag,min_secs,max_secs}, image_grading_{enabled,eccentricity_threshold}, calibration.{auto_calibrate,auto_dark_from_library}, dark_library.temp_tolerance, adaptive_swap.score_weights, preflight_strictness, polar_alignment_max_age_days. No case of the UI showing one value and the DB holding another.
coverage_note: All 11 sections named in my scope were opened and driven in the running app; every enumerated settings unit in my scope is in units_visited except the two listed in units_unreached (focus-model, which is unreachable by construction and is itself reported as a defect, and the populated state of captured-images, which needs a remote appliance). Method: fresh profile via drive_linux.py start --fresh, Skip onboarding, then screenshot -> read -> click-xy on every control, with sqlite3 against /tmp/ns-audit/settings-imaging/data/skotiq.db after each change to check the UI against storage. Defaults were re-verified on a genuinely fresh seed after I discovered the pre-existing profile had been mutated by an earlier agent (e.g. it showed adaptive reference mag 24.0 and image grading ON, whereas the shipped defaults are 21.5 and OFF) - every 'default' claim above is from the fresh seed or default_settings.dart, not the contaminated profile. Two things limited me. (1) Desktop 'Snapshot' is preview-only (badge 'Preview only', Session 'Captured 0 frames', empty capture directory), so I could not make a frame hit disk to observe the naming-pattern failure end to end; that finding is marked with exactly what was and was not observed. Getting there needs a full sequence run, which belongs to the sequencer sweep - worth handing off as 'run one Expose node with file_naming_pattern=$TARGET_$BANANA and confirm the run aborts'. (2) Mid-audit my Xvfb :82 and app process were killed by something outside this agent (both vanished together); I restarted fresh and re-verified everything that mattered on the clean profile, and I also lost ~15 minutes to a scratchpad helper script being overwritten by a concurrent agent, which briefly pointed my screenshots at another agent's display - two screenshots taken during that window (settings-imaging-60/61) are of the 'planning' profile and are not cited as evidence anywhere. Not attempted, and worth a follow-up: the Image Grading 'Reject folder path' behaviour with an absolute path outside the capture root, and the Calibration Library tag/share/delete dialogs, which need at least one master in the library to reach. The app was stopped cleanly at the end (drive_linux.py stop --profile settings-imaging).
